forms: pick the wind instrument from a list
say how an instrument is played
match an instrument to its community
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G5.CREATI.WIND_MUSICAL_INSTRUMENTS..mastery: The child names the nzumari and the siwa (Swahili coast) and the animal horn, flute and whistle as wind instruments, knows a wind instrument makes its sound when the player blows air into it, and does not put the nyatiti, orutu, litungu or ngoma in the wind group. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: name the part from its job
say what blowing, the tube and the finger holes each do
say why uncovering holes raises the sound
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G5.CREATI.WIND_MUSICAL_INSTRUMENTS..mastery: The child says the mouthpiece is where the player blows in, the air inside the tube is what vibrates to make the sound, the finger holes change the length of the vibrating air (more holes covered gives a lower sound, fewer covered a higher sound) and the open end lets the sound out. The child does not say the wood itself sings. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the right way to clean or store it
say why a care step matters
choose the careful action in a story
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G5.CREATI.WIND_MUSICAL_INSTRUMENTS..mastery: The child cleans the mouthpiece before another player uses the instrument, keeps the instrument dry and away from rain and hot sun, stores it in a safe place, and handles it gently, and gives the reason for each step. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say what cross-hatching is for
put the etching steps in order
pick the tool that scratches
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G5.CREATI.WIND_MUSICAL_INSTRUMENTS..mastery: The child says cross-hatching is lines that cross each other to make texture and dark areas, and puts the etching steps in order: colour the paper with bright crayons, cover with dark crayon, scratch the picture through the dark layer with a pointed tool so the bright colours show. This is the knowledge half of outcome e; drawing it is practical. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the part of the foot for a kick or stop
say how a straight dribble is done
pick the careful action in a story
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G5.CREATI.FOOTBALL.SKILLS.mastery: The child says an instep kick uses the laces (top) of the foot, an outside-of-the-foot kick uses the outer side of the foot, stopping uses the inside of the foot, a step trap puts the sole on top of the ball, and a straight dribble pushes the ball forward in small touches with the head up. This is the knowledge half of outcome a; doing it is practical. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: put the steps in order
say why a step is needed
pick the material for a step
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G5.CREATI.FOOTBALL.PAPIER_MACHE.mastery: The child puts the steps in order: shred paper, soak it in water, pound it to a pulp, mix the pulp with an adhesive such as flour paste, press it onto the cone mould, let it dry fully, then remove it. The child knows each step has a reason. This is the knowledge half of outcomes b and c; making the cones is practical. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say the beats of a note or rest
say how a note looks in words
add the beats of a short pattern
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G5.CREATI.RHYTHM.VALUES.mastery: The child says a minim lasts two beats, a crotchet one beat, a pair of quavers one beat together (half a beat each), and each rest is silent for as long as its note. Questions describe shapes, signs and holes in words, because the phone question has no staff or picture. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: match a French name to a note
say how many sounds a name has
pick the name for a described symbol
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G5.CREATI.RHYTHM.NAMES.mastery: The child matches taa-aa to the minim (two beats), taa to the crotchet (one beat) and ta-te to a pair of quavers (two sounds in one beat), and knows a rest is silent: it is counted but not sounded. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the pattern that fills two beats
say which beat is strong
count beats and not sounds
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G5.CREATI.RHYTHM.TWO_BEAT.mastery: The child counts beats and not sounds, so ta-te ta-te is two beats (four sounds), knows a two-beat pattern is counted 1 2 with the strong beat on 1, and picks patterns whose notes add up to two beats. This is the knowledge half of outcomes e and f; clapping and composing are practical. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the primary colours
pick the secondary colours
say whether a colour is primary or secondary
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G5.CREATI.PAINTING_AND_MOSAIC.COLOU.mastery: The child names red, yellow and blue as the primary colours (not made by mixing) and orange, green and purple as the secondary colours (made by mixing two primaries), and does not call green, black or white primary. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say what two colours make a secondary
say what a mix of two primaries makes
pick the pair for a needed colour
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G5.CREATI.PAINTING_AND_MOSAIC.MIXIN.mastery: The child says red and yellow make orange, blue and yellow make green, and red and blue make purple, and picks the right pair when a painter needs one of them. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say how a wash is painted
put the steps of a scenery in order
say which brush and paint suit a wash
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G5.CREATI.PAINTING_AND_MOSAIC.WASH.mastery: The child says a wash uses thin, watery paint spread in broad strokes with a large brush, light colours go on first (the sky) and darker colours and small details go on last, after the wash has dried. This is the knowledge half of outcome b; painting is practical. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say what a mosaic is made of
put the mosaic steps in order
pick a material that suits a mosaic
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G5.CREATI.PAINTING_AND_MOSAIC.MOSAI.mastery: The child says a mosaic picture is made by sticking many small pieces (coloured paper, seeds, bottle tops, small stones or tile pieces) close together on a surface with small gaps, after drawing the design first, and glues a small area at a time. This is the knowledge half of outcomes c and d; making it is practical. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the next syllable going up or down
say which syllable is highest or lowest
put the five syllables in order
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G5.CREATI.MELODY.SOLFA.mastery: The child puts d r m f s in order from the lowest sound to the highest (d lowest, s highest), says the order backwards for going down, and does not treat the first syllable sung as the highest. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say which syllable a described sign shows
say how a syllable's sign looks
say how the height of the hand changes
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G5.CREATI.MELODY.SIGNS.mastery: The child says d is a closed fist held low, r is a hand sloping upward, m is a flat hand with the palm down, f is the thumb pointing down, s is a flat hand with the palm facing sideways, and that the hands are held higher as the pitch gets higher. Questions describe shapes, signs and holes in words, because the phone question has no staff or picture. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: name the technique used in a short melody
say what a technique means
pick the melody that uses a technique
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G5.CREATI.MELODY.TECHNIQUES.mastery: The child reads a melody written as d r m f s letters and names stepwise motion (to the next syllable), a narrow leap (skipping one syllable), repetition of a pitch, variation of a pitch, and an ending on a long note. This is the knowledge half of outcome c; composing is practical. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: name the part from its job
say which part hits the ball
pick the feature of a good rounders bat
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G5.CREATI.ROUNDERS.BAT.mastery: The child names the knob (the end that stops the bat slipping from the hand), the handle and grip (where it is held), and the head (the rounded, thicker hitting part), and knows a rounders bat is smooth and rounded, not flat like a cricket bat. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the tool for a carving job
pick the wood that suits
pick the safe carving action
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G5.CREATI.ROUNDERS.CARVING.mastery: The child pairs the saw with cutting the wood to length, the knife or rasp with shaping, and sandpaper with smoothing, says dry hardwood suits a bat, and cuts away from the body with the wood held steady and an adult watching. This is the knowledge half of outcomes b and c; carving is practical. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the safe action at the batting post
say why a safety rule matters
say what to do in a game story
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G5.CREATI.ROUNDERS.SAFETY.mastery: The child stands well away from the batter, does not swing the bat when others are near, puts the bat down and never throws it, bowls underarm to the batter and not at a person, and says each rule protects someone. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say what the receiver does in each change
say which way the baton moves into the hand
say why a baton change method matters
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G5.PERFOR.ATHLETICS.BATON.mastery: The child says that in a visual change the receiver looks back and watches the baton come into the hand, in a non-visual change the receiver keeps looking ahead and puts the hand back on a signal, an upsweep moves the baton upward into the hand and a downsweep moves it downward, and that both keep the receiver running without slowing. This is the knowledge half of outcomes c and d. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say where the baton must be passed
say what to do when a baton is dropped
pick the safe action in a race story
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G5.PERFOR.ATHLETICS.RELAY.mastery: The child says the baton is passed inside the exchange zone and carried by hand, never thrown, the runner who drops it picks it up, runners keep to their lane, and the team wins when its last runner crosses the line with the baton. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: put the plaiting steps in order
say how many strands and why
pick a plaiting material
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G5.PERFOR.ATHLETICS.PLAITING.mastery: The child says a plait uses three strands of equal length, fixed together at the top, with the outer strand crossed over the middle strand from the right and then from the left in turn, pulled to an even tightness and tied off at the end. Sisal, leather strips and strips of old fabric are plaiting materials. This is the knowledge half of outcome b. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: name the technique from how it is done
say how a technique makes its pattern
pick the technique that suits a job
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G5.PERFOR.FABRIC_DECORATION.DECOR_T.mastery: The child says tie and dye makes a pattern by tying parts of the cloth so the dye cannot reach them, appliqué sews or sticks cut shapes of one fabric onto another, batik uses wax to keep dye out, and embroidery uses thread stitches, and does not swap tie and dye with appliqué. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: put the steps in order
say what the tied part looks like after dyeing
say how to keep safe with dye
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G5.PERFOR.FABRIC_DECORATION.TIE_DYE.mastery: The child puts the steps in order: wet the cloth, pinch and tie it tightly, dye it, rinse, untie, then dry in the shade. The child knows the tied parts keep the cloth's own colour, dye is fixed with a fastener such as salt, and gloves and an adult are needed with dye. This is the knowledge half of outcome b. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: put the appliqué steps in order
pick the material for a step
say what holds the shape on
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G5.PERFOR.FABRIC_DECORATION.APPLIQU.mastery: The child says appliqué means cutting shapes from another fabric, placing them on a background cloth (pinned or tacked first), and sewing or sticking round the edges so they stay on, and that the background cloth is not cut away. This is the knowledge half of outcome c. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the community of a dance
pick the occasion of a dance
say who does what in a performance
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G5.PERFOR.KENYAN_FOLK_DANCE.BACKGRO.mastery: The child matches isukuti to the Luhya, adumu to the Maasai, mwomboko to the Kikuyu, chakacha to the Swahili of the coast and ohangla to the Luo, gives an occasion for each, and says the soloist leads the song, the chorus answers, instrumentalists play and dancers dance. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: name the component from a described example
sort examples into components
say what a component adds to the dance
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G5.PERFOR.KENYAN_FOLK_DANCE.COMPONE.mastery: The child names songs, body movements, costumes (clothes worn), ornaments (beads, anklets), body adornment (paint, hairstyle), formations (circle, line), props (things held) and instruments (drums, horns), and does not swap ornament with costume or prop with instrument. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick a role of folk dance
pick the statement that is not a role
say which role fits a story
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G5.PERFOR.KENYAN_FOLK_DANCE.ROLES.mastery: The child gives roles such as entertainment, handing down culture and values, bringing people together, marking events like weddings and harvests, and earning an income for performers, and does not say a folk dance is only for fun or only for old people. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the safe action before dancing
pick the respectful action
say what to do in a rehearsal story
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G5.PERFOR.KENYAN_FOLK_DANCE.DANCE_S.mastery: The child warms up before dancing, clears stones and sharp things from the space, keeps ornaments secure, waits for a turn, listens to the leader, and respects the dances of other communities and does not laugh at them. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the glove puppet from a description
say how a puppet is moved
say what a puppet type is called
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G5.PERFOR.PUPPETRY.TYPES.mastery: The child says a glove puppet is worn over the hand with the fingers moving the head and arms, a finger puppet fits on one finger, a string puppet hangs on strings, a rod puppet moves on sticks, and a shadow puppet is a flat shape seen behind a lit screen. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the recyclable material
say what to use for a part
say why the size must fit the hand
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G5.PERFOR.PUPPETRY.MAKE.mastery: The child says recyclable materials are things already used that can be used again (old socks, paper bags, cardboard, bottle tops, cloth scraps), picks one for a part such as eyes or hair, and says the puppet must fit the hand so the fingers can move the head and arms. This is the knowledge half of outcome b. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say what a puppet show needs
say what a topical song is
pick the right action in a show story
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G5.PERFOR.PUPPETRY.SHOW.mastery: The child says a puppet show needs a screen that hides the puppeteers, a story, a different voice for each character, and only the speaking puppet moving, and that a topical song is about an issue the community is talking about, such as hygiene, road safety or looking after trees. This is the knowledge half of outcome c. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: put the notes in order of pitch
say how many fingers G, A or B needs
say whether a note is higher or lower
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G5.PERFOR.DESCANT_RECORDER.NOTES.mastery: The child puts the notes in order from the lowest, G, A, B, then the higher C and D (C1 and D1), says B covers the thumb hole and one finger, A the thumb and two fingers, G the thumb and three fingers, and that covering more holes gives a lower note. This is the knowledge half of outcome a; playing is practical. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the way to hold and finger the recorder
say how to blow for a good tone
say what tonguing does
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G5.PERFOR.DESCANT_RECORDER.TECHNIQU.mastery: The child covers each hole fully with the soft pad of the finger, blows a gentle steady breath (too hard gives a shrill squeak), starts each note by tonguing softly with a "too" sound, and knows a good tone is clear and smooth. This is the knowledge half of outcome b. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say what the arms do
say what the legs do
say how to breathe
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G5.PERFOR.SWIMMING.CRAWL.mastery: The child says the body lies flat on the front with the face in the water, the arms pull one after the other (one under the water while the other swings over it), the legs kick up and down in small quick flutter kicks from the hips, and the swimmer breathes out in the water and turns the head to the side to breathe in. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the safe or clean action
say why a pool rule matters
say what to do in a pool story
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G5.PERFOR.SWIMMING.POOL_SAFETY.mastery: The child showers before getting in, never swims alone and swims only when a teacher or lifeguard is watching, does not run on the pool side, does not push, and checks the depth and enters feet first when not sure. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick a counting game
say what a counting game trains
say how rhythm joins a counting game
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G5.PERFOR.SWIMMING.COUNTING_GAMES.mastery: The child names bao (a board game of pits and seeds) and counting rhymes, skipping and clapping games as counting games, says that counting games train counting, planning and teamwork and the moving ones build fitness, and that rhythm means counting and moving to the beat. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the helpful, respectful comment
say what to look at in an artwork
say what to do in a gallery walk
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G5.APPREC.ANALYSIS_OF_CREATIVE_ART..mastery: The child comments on the type of art, the materials and what stands out (colour, line, shape, texture), says what they like and why, offers one polite idea to improve, and does not touch other people's work or use rude words. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the word that fits a description
say what a word means
